sentence: This project tests how well and how safely alpha-emitter therapy works against osteosarcoma that has spread, using pet dogs with naturally occurring cancer.
This project tries to work out how genes are switched on and off inside single cells.
This project builds a way to deliver a skin cancer vaccine to lymph nodes and tests whether it triggers strong, lasting immune responses against melanoma.
This project runs a shared lab that provides instruments and viruses used to deliver genes for research on the eye.
This project uses live imaging in tiny agarose wells to watch how single-celled parasites change between stages of their life cycle.
This project builds a shared data and modeling resource to study how tumors respond to and resist radiation in brain and nerve cancers of children.
This project studies what triggers smoking lapses in the moment among adults who smoke menthol cigarettes and are trying to quit.
This project buys a brain scanner that lets researchers take very sharp pictures of the human brain and small brain structures.
This project studies how Polycomb complexes work in human health and disease, including cancer and neurodevelopmental disorders.
This project provides mouse models of lung transplant and tissue tests to find the molecular pathways behind failure of a transplanted lung.
This project runs a shared lab that offers DNA and RNA sequencing and single cell analysis to cancer researchers.
This project keeps building a software tool that helps researchers analyze brain signals recorded from people.
This project tests whether changing a channel in brain support cells called astrocytes can protect blood flow, metabolism and memory in a type of dementia.
This project uses deep learning to design proteins that could help the body make antibodies against HIV-1 for a vaccine.
This project studies how the HIV-1 capsid interacts with the viral RNA genome when new virus particles are put together.
This project studies how key gut microbes shape the growth, specialization and fat-burning function of cells lining the intestine.
This project tests whether the hormone prolactin changes how the brain hears baby cries so that parents respond with care.
This project builds a monkey model of HIV in the brain and tests whether CRISPR gene editing can clear the virus.
This project builds an imaging and computer tool that quickly analyzes tissue samples to show how gene changes affect the growth of glial cells.
This project studies how immune cells control production of a small RNA that acts as a brake on inflammation.
